findings.title: Double-backtick escapes meant to show literal backticks render as broken KaTeX math
locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:2273 — "list-leader continuation inside an open `` `` `` span"

docs/build/architecture.html — same row renders $```math$, \]\(@ref[^)]*\)\ followed by a bare stray backtick, two split spans plus literal "RULE.DOC.ARG_BULLET` silences\u2026", $$ `` (twice), and $`[^`]*[\u2264\u2026]*`$
findings.description: This build's Documenter/KaTeX setup treats a code span delimited by exactly two backticks as inline math (per the rendered policy's own RULE.TEX.RENDERED_MATH: "Inline math is a double-backtick span"). Seven places in the source text try to show a literal backtick, a backtick-delimited regex, or the project's own ``/```math fence syntax as a worked example, using the classic Markdown trick of a wider or padded backtick delimiter around inner backticks. Because the outer delimiter still measures to a 2-backtick run (or, for SCAN.REF_ABUT_CODE/SCAN.ARG_BULLET_BOLD, a single backtick abutting a literal inner backtick that prematurely closes the span), Documenter hands the content to KaTeX as a formula; a backtick is not valid LaTeX, so KaTeX's fallback leaves the raw, undelimited math source ($`n`$, $```math$, bare $$ with a stray `` left over, split <code> tags plus dangling backtick text, or the whole regex wrapped in $\u2026$) sitting in the rendered prose. None of this is visible from the Markdown/docstring source alone — reading src/Reflection.jl or docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, the intent reads as plain code formatting; the defect exists only in what Documenter actually produced. Three of the seven instances are, ironically, ARCHITECTURE.md's own worked examples of the very math-notation rule they sit inside (RENDERED_MATH, INLINE_MATH_SPLIT, FORMULA_IN_BACKTICKS, ABUTTING_SPANS rows of the scan catalogue), and none of it is caught by SCAN.HTML_RENDERED_MARKUP, which only scans built HTML for surviving `*`/`__` emphasis markers, not stray `$`.
findings.resolution_hint: For each location, stop trying to nest backticks inside a 2-backtick-fenced span: either drop to a single plain backtick around a backtick-free literal (`n`, `n = 2`), or describe the delimiter in prose ("a double-backtick span") instead of showing it literally, or use a fenced code block for the regex examples. Rebuild the docs and grep docs/build for `<span>$` containing a backtick to confirm the class is gone.

findings.title: Four live CLI verbs (bump, fleet, release, selftest) are documented nowhere on the built site
locations: docs/build/guide/verbs.html — opens "the table is closed, and every verb below is rendered from its own docstring" yet lists none of these four
docs/src/guide/verbs.md, docs/src/api/CLI.md — no `@docs` block anywhere names Bump, Fleet, Release or Selftest (grep for the four words is empty)
docs/build/architecture.html §3 — the only site-wide mention is the bare filenames "Doctor.jl Sync.jl Init.jl Fleet.jl Bump.jl Release.jl Install.jl", not a documented verb
findings.description: All four are real, currently-registered entries of the closed VERBS table (confirmed by grepping every `VERBS["..."] = ` assignment across src/CLI/*.jl: 21 verbs registered, only these four absent from every `@docs` block on the site) and each already carries a complete docstring in source. guide/verbs.html's own opening sentence claims to be the closed, drift-proof table of every verb "rendered from its own docstring so the page cannot drift from the code" — exactly the claim this omission falsifies, since the gap is a missing `@docs` entry, not a hand-copy that drifted. A reader who only reads the built docs cannot discover that `gbg bump`, `gbg fleet`, `gbg release` or `gbg selftest` exist at all. This is visible only by cross-checking the built site's page-by-page @docs coverage against the live VERBS registry in src/ — no single page (nor the source alone) shows the gap.
findings.resolution_hint: Add `GBGCodingTools.cmd_bump` (or `bump`), `GBGCodingTools.Fleet` and its verb function, `GBGCodingTools.cmd_release` and `GBGCodingTools.cmd_selftest` to an `@docs` block in docs/src/guide/verbs.md (matching the existing "Machine and self" / "Consumer setup" grouping), rebuild, and confirm all four bindings now appear under docs/build.

findings.title: The module map on the home page has no entry for the scan engine
locations: docs/build/index.html — the `GBGCodingTools` module docstring lists main, Config, makedocs, TestHarness/Reflection/Witnesses, TreeHash, HtmlWalker, and "The CLI files under src/CLI/" as the whole map
src/Scan.jl:19,41,67,133,385,477,498 — struct Hit, struct ScanResult, register_scan!, prose_lines, scan_docs, scan_html, write_public_surface are all defined here, at top level, not under src/CLI/
docs/build/api/CLI.html — Hit, ScanResult, register_scan!, prose_lines, consolidate and write_public_surface are documented under an "Engines" heading with no link from the module map
findings.description: RULE.DOC.MODULE_MAP requires the module docstring to list one linked one-liner per operation family; RULE.DOC.CURRENT treats a summary naming only a subset of what the code now provides as stale even where every sentence is literally true. `src/Scan.jl` is the deterministic text/HTML scan engine (`gbg scan docs`/`gbg scan html`, the `Hit` and `ScanResult` types, `register_scan!`, `prose_lines`, `write_public_surface`) — a distinct operation family with its own catalogue (`catalog/scans.toml`) and its own two CLI verbs — but it is neither under `src/CLI/` (so the map's one catch-all CLI bullet does not cover it) nor named by any other bullet. The engine does have a home elsewhere on the site (CLI.html, verbs.html), so this is a map-completeness gap rather than a missing-documentation gap.
findings.resolution_hint: Add one bullet to the `GBGCodingTools` module docstring in src/GBGCodingTools.jl naming the scan engine, e.g. "`Hit`, `ScanResult`, [`scan_docs`](@ref), [`scan_html`](@ref) — the deterministic text/HTML scan engine over `catalog/scans.toml`", then rebuild.
